inline_comments.comment: This file is an LLM prompt / development scratch note that should not be committed to the repository. It documents implementation instructions for the tidy-tree algorithm and has no value to other contributors. Delete before merging. Note that `.gitignore` adds `.instructions/` (a directory), not `instructions.md` (a root-level file), so this file is not currently ignored.

Developer scratch/test HTML file committed at the repo root. Per the project rules, verify that developer playground files have not been accidentally committed. This file also references `http://localhost:9000/mermaid.js` (a hardcoded local server URL) and should be deleted before merging.
Scratch `.mmd` test file committed to the source tree. This is a development artifact that should not be checked in. Delete before merging.

The ELK layout is being hard-coded into mermaid core via a relative cross-package path:
```typescript
loader: async () => await import('../../../mermaid-layout-elk/src/render.js'),
```
This defeats the entire purpose of `@mermaid-js/layout-elk` being a separate opt-in package (as documented in its own README). It bundles ELK into the core mermaid bundle for every user, regardless of whether they need it. ELK should remain consumer-registered via `mermaid.registerLayoutLoaders()` and should not be registered here. Remove this entry.

This silently overrides the layout to `'tidy-tree'` for all mindmaps that do not explicitly specify a layout, contradicting the `layoutAlgorithm` schema default of `'cose-bilkent'` and the fallback `'cose-bilkent'` hard-coded in `mindmapRenderer.ts`. This is a breaking behavioral change for existing mindmaps — users who relied on cose-bilkent positioning will get a completely different layout without any opt-in. The default should be consistent with the schema, and the decision about which algorithm to use should be made in the renderer, not during preprocessing.

`_drawNodes` and `_updateNodeDimensions` are defined but never called anywhere in the new renderer. `drawNode` is also imported but only used by the dead `_drawNodes` function. These are all dead code left over from an earlier iteration. Remove them.

This file is inside the `mermaid` package but imports its types from the `'mermaid'` package itself:
```typescript
import type { InternalHelpers, LayoutData, RenderOptions, SVG, SVGGroup } from 'mermaid';
```
This is a circular self-reference. The dagre layout (the established pattern for in-package layouts) uses relative imports exclusively — e.g., `import { log } from '../../../logger.js'`. Use relative imports here instead. The same issue exists in `tidy-tree/render.ts`.

This test file imports `layout` and `validateLayoutData` from `./index.js`, but `cose-bilkent/index.ts` only exports `render`. Neither `layout` nor `validateLayoutData` is re-exported from `index.ts`. Additionally, `MindmapLayoutData` is imported from `./types.js`, but that file defines only `PositionedNode`, `PositionedEdge`, `LayoutResult`, and `CytoscapeLayoutConfig` — no `MindmapLayoutData`. These tests will fail to compile and run.

The test assertions use bare numeric string IDs (e.g., `'0'`, `'1'`) to find nodes and check edge `start`/`end` values, but `flattenNodes` generates IDs with the `'node_'` prefix (`'node_0'`, `'node_1'`, etc.) and `generateEdges` likewise uses `start: 'node_' + node.id.toString()`. Every assertion in this file that looks up a node or edge by ID will fail. For example:
```typescript
// Fails — actual ID is 'node_0'
result.nodes.find((n: any) => n.id === '0')
// Fails — actual start is 'node_0'
result.edges.find((e) => e.start === '0' && e.end === '1')
```
Either strip the prefix in the implementation or update all assertions to use `'node_0'`, `'node_1'`, etc.

`let intersectionShift = 50` is a module-level mutable variable that is reassigned inside `executeTidyTreeLayout` on every call (`intersectionShift = 30`). Per the project rules, module-level mutable variables in layout/rendering modules leak state across parallel diagram renders. Move `intersectionShift` inside `executeTidyTreeLayout` as a `const`, and if it needs to be configurable, pass it via `_config` or the diagram config.

`_maxChildren` is computed but never used:
```typescript
const _maxChildren = Math.max(...data.nodes.map((node) => node.children?.length ?? 0));
```
Additionally, `node.children` does not exist on the flat `Node` type in `types.ts`, so this would always yield `0` via the `?? 0` fallback. The related commented-out code (`// if (maxChildren > 5)`) should be removed or tracked as a GitHub issue. Remove this dead computation.

`fixCorners` (along with `extractCornerPoints` and `findAdjacentPoint`) is removed from shared edge rendering and replaced with `adjustForArrowHeads`. This affects edge rendering for **all diagram types**, not just mindmaps. The PR description only mentions mindmap layout changes and diamond offset fixes. Removing `fixCorners` is a significant regression risk for other diagrams (e.g., flowcharts with orthogonal routing). This change needs explicit justification, separate testing across all affected diagram types, and ideally its own PR.
`createGraphWithElements` is exported but not imported anywhere in the codebase. This is dead code. Either wire it up to a consumer or remove the file.

Multiple `log.debug('APA01 ...')` development trace statements were added throughout the ELK renderer (edges loop, graph structure dump, validation loop, try/catch, and layout result). Per project guidelines, remove all debug logging with development-specific prefixes before merging. Use `log.debug` sparingly and only for information that is useful in production diagnostics, not for step-by-step algorithm tracing.
The entire function body is wrapped in an unnecessary bare block `{ ... }`. This adds one level of indentation throughout the function with no semantic effect. Remove the extra braces.

The file now contains more than 10 `<pre id="diagram4">` elements, all sharing the same `id`. Duplicate IDs are invalid HTML and will cause unpredictable behavior since `document.getElementById('diagram4')` will only return the first match. This is a developer scratch file and should not be committed in this state — but if it is kept, each diagram element needs a unique ID.

`buildSubTree` generates virtual root IDs using `Math.random()`:
```typescript
id: `virtual-root-${Math.random()}`,
```
Non-deterministic IDs make diagrams non-reproducible across renders and break snapshot/regression tests. Use a counter or hash based on the input data instead.

`getData()` generates a non-deterministic `diagramId`:
```typescript
diagramId: 'mindmap-' + Date.now(),
```
This changes on every call, which is problematic for SVG elements that reference the diagram ID (e.g., marker refs). In `mindmapRenderer.ts`, `data4Layout.diagramId = id` overwrites this immediately anyway, making the `Date.now()` call in `getData()` pointless. Remove it from `getData()` and rely on the renderer to set the correct ID.

The four new tests are all titled `'Bang and cloud shape with <layout> layout'`, but none of the test diagrams actually use bang (`))...((`) or cloud (`)...(`") shapes — they're all plain mindmaps with default node types. The test names are copy-paste artifacts from the existing test suite and should be updated to accurately describe what is being tested (e.g., `'default mindmap with dagre layout'`).

general_comments.comment: **Changeset is wrong in level and scope.** The `.changeset/hungry-guests-drive.md` file claims this is a `patch` fix for `@mermaid-js/layout-elk` with description "Updated offset calculations for diamond shape when handling intersections." In reality this PR adds multiple entirely new layout algorithms (tidy-tree, cose-bilkent as a registered layout), changes the default mindmap rendering engine, modifies shared edge rendering for all diagrams, and adds new shape types. This is a `minor` feature release, and changes to the `mermaid` package itself need their own changeset entry. The current changeset would generate incorrect release notes and wrong semver bumps.

**`cose-bilkent` layout tests are structurally broken.** `layout.test.ts` imports `layout` and `validateLayoutData` from `./index.js` and `MindmapLayoutData` from `./types.js`. None of these symbols exist at those import sites — `index.ts` only re-exports `render`, and `types.ts` has no `MindmapLayoutData`. These tests will fail at import resolution before a single `it()` block runs. A separate issue: `validateLayoutData` in `layout.ts` has no `rootNode` check, but the test expects `'Root node is required'` to be thrown when `rootNode` is `null`. The test validates behavior that the implementation does not provide.

**Debug artifacts throughout the codebase.** The following should be cleaned up before merging: (1) All `log.debug('APA01 ...')` / `log.debug('APA12 ...')` development trace lines in the ELK renderer and mindmap renderer. (2) Commented-out `console.log` blocks (e.g., in `question.ts`, `intersect-line.js`, `tidy-tree/render.ts`). (3) A `// debugger;` comment in `tidy-tree/render.ts`. (4) Commented-out alternative implementations (`// lineData = fixCorners(lineData)` in `edges.js`, the commented-out `points` array in `tidy-tree/render.ts`). Per project rules, committed code should not contain debug console statements or development-era commented-out code.

**Magic numbers in tidy-tree layout should be named constants or config properties.** Values like `gap = 20`, `bottomPadding = 40`, `intersectionShift = 30`, `treeSpacing = rootNode.width / 2 + 30`, and the `+ 20` root Y-offset are scattered through `layout.ts` without explanation. Per project rules, extract layout geometry into named constants at the top of the relevant scope, and for values that users may want to tune, expose them in the mindmap diagram config (following the `pieDb.ts` pattern).

**`chokidar` downgrade is undocumented.** Both `package.json` and `packages/mermaid/package.json` downgrade `chokidar` from `^4.0.3` to `^3.6.0`. The PR description gives no reason for this. Chokidar 4.x dropped `readdirp` as a dependency (seen in the lockfile diff). If something in this PR requires v3 compatibility, it should be explained with a comment or in the PR description; otherwise this downgrade should be reverted and tracked separately.
